skills.name: Accounting for transactions with commercial containers

note.text:
Commercial containers (emballages) such as crates, bottles and gas cylinders may be returnable. The customer pays a deposit (consignation) when goods are delivered in them and gets it back when they are returned.
Seller:
• Goods delivered with consigned containers: debit 411 Customers (goods TTC + deposit), credit 701 Sales and 443 VAT, and credit 4194 Customers, consigned containers (deposit). No VAT is charged on the deposit.
• Containers returned: debit 4194, credit 411 (or 571 if refunded in cash) with the deposit refunded.
Buyer: debit 4094 Suppliers, containers to be returned with the deposit paid; on return, credit 4094.
Containers not returned are treated as sold (or bought).

sections.heading: Returnable containers
sections.text:
Many goods come in returnable containers: crates of soft drinks and beer, gas cylinders, drums. The seller charges a deposit (consignation) to make sure the containers come back. When they are returned, the deposit is refunded.
The deposit is not income and no VAT is charged on it: it is money the seller must give back.

sections.heading: The seller's entries
sections.text:
• Containers delivered: debit {'411 Customers'}, credit {'4194 Customers, consigned containers'} with the deposits.
• Containers returned: debit {'4194'}, credit {'411 Customers'} (or {'571 Cash'} if refunded in cash).
Example: {20} crates at {500} FCFA = {10000} FCFA in deposits; {15} returned → refund {7500} FCFA.

sections.heading: The buyer's entries and unreturned containers
sections.text:
The buyer records deposits paid in {'4094 Suppliers, containers to be returned'}: debit when paid, credit when the containers go back.
Containers that are not returned are treated as sold by the seller and bought by the buyer.
Keeping track of deposits avoids losing money on missing crates.

key_words.meaning: packaging such as crates, bottles and cylinders
money paid for returnable containers, refunded on return
seller's account for deposits on consigned containers
buyer's account for deposits paid on containers

mistake.wrong: Container deposits are credited to {'701'} Sales
mistake.right: They are credited to {'4194'} Customers, consigned containers
mistake.why: A deposit is refundable, so it is a debt, not income.

worked_example.problem: A drinks depot delivers drinks with {n} crates; the deposit is {dep} FCFA per crate. Find the deposit and the entry for it.
steps: Deposit = {n} × {dep} = {n * dep} FCFA (no VAT on the deposit).
Debit {'411 Customers'} {n * dep}; credit {'4194 Customers, consigned containers'} {n * dep}.

cards.idea: Deposit = number of containers × deposit per container.
The seller credits {'4194'} with deposits received; no VAT on deposits.
Returned containers are refunded; unreturned ones are treated as sold.

check.prompt: A customer received {n} crates (deposit {d} FCFA each) and returns {r} of them. How much deposit is refunded (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: Only the {r} returned crates are refunded.
That is the value of the crates not returned.

questions.prompt: A brewery depot delivers {n} crates with a deposit of {d} FCFA each. What is the total deposit (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: No VAT is charged on container deposits.

pick.q: Deposits of 10 000 FCFA are charged to a customer for crates delivered.
pick.r: Dr 411 Customers / Cr 4194 Customers, consigned containers
pick.y: The deposit is a debt to the customer until the crates come back.

pick.q: The customer returns the crates and the 10 000 FCFA deposit is credited back to his account.
pick.r: Dr 4194 Customers, consigned containers / Cr 411 Customers
e: The deposit is refunded, not sold.
pick.y: The debt to the customer is cancelled.

pick.q: Cash is refunded to a customer who brings back crates worth 6 000 FCFA in deposits.
pick.r: Dr 4194 Customers, consigned containers / Cr 571 Cash
e: Cash goes out, so Cash is credited.
The deposit is refunded, not sold.
pick.y: Refund in cash cancels the deposit debt.

questions.prompt: Which entry does the SELLER make? {X.q}
A customer received {n} crates (deposit {d} FCFA each) and returns {r} of them. How much deposit is refunded (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: Only the {r} returned crates are refunded.
That is the value of the crates not returned.

pick.q: Which account does the BUYER debit when paying a deposit on containers to be returned?
e: The deposit is not a purchase of goods.
pick.y: The supplier owes the buyer the deposit back.

pick.q: Why is no VAT charged on the deposit for returnable crates?
pick.r: The deposit is refundable, not a sale of the crates
pick.y: Only if the crates are kept do they become a sale.

pick.q: A customer keeps 5 crates instead of returning them. How are they treated?
pick.r: As a sale of containers to the customer
pick.y: Unreturned containers are treated as sold (or bought).
